chunks: Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abdal ibn Malik, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Kahili, from Mu'adh, the seller of garments, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to milk the goat of his family.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad do with his family's goat?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Prophet’s (PBUH) personal engagement in domestic labor, specifically milking his family's goat, which underscores the virtue of humility and the rejection of aristocratic detachment in Shia tradition. It serves as a practical model for the Imams and the faithful to balance spiritual leadership with active participation in household duties, reinforcing the sanctity of everyday work.
